title: Brentius takes justification to include renovation; Protestants spare him
source_text: XXXII. Imo inter Theologos Confessionis Augustanae celeberrimus Joh. Brentius ita accipit vocem justificationis, sub qua hominis renovationem comprehendi existimavit, eamque suam sententiam Epistola ad Melancthonem hac de re scripta testatus est, ut patet ex Melancthonis ad ipsum responsione, quae legitur in Consiliis ejusdem Melancthonis, pag. 245. Imaginaris, inquit ad Brentium, fide justificari homines, quia fide accipiamus Spiritum Sanctum, ut postea justi esse possimus; videlicet, impletione legis, quam efficit in nobis Spiritus Sanctus. Neque tamen propterea quisquam Protestantium gravioris censurae notandum putavit Brentium. Quem, inquit Johannes Gerardus, ut propterea erroris Pontificii de justificatione reum suspicari velimus, quod termino justificationis, in latiori significatione, Latinae vocis compositionem secutus utatur. Loc. Theol. tom. 3. cap. de Justit. per fidem, num. 245. ubi prolixum citat Brentii hac de re locum, ex ejus Apologia Confessionis Wirtembergensis, de Justificatione.
pass_a_gloss: Nay, among the theologians of the Augsburg Confession the most celebrated John Brentius so takes the word of justification, under which he thought man's renovation to be comprehended, and testified that opinion of his in a letter to Melanchthon written on this matter, as appears from Melanchthon's reply to him, which is read in the Consilia of the same Melanchthon, p. 245. You imagine, he says to Brentius, that men are justified by faith because by faith we receive the Holy Spirit so that afterward we can be just—namely by the fulfillment of the law which the Holy Spirit works in us. Yet on that account no Protestant thought Brentius ought to be marked with a heavier censure. Whom, says John Gerhard, as if on that account we should wish to suspect him guilty of the Pontifical error on justification, because he uses the term of justification in a wider signification, following the Latin composition of the word. Loc. Theol. tom. 3 cap. on Righteousness by faith, n. 245, where he cites a lengthy place of Brentius on this matter from his Apology of the Württemberg Confession, on Justification.
pass_b_english: Brentius folded renovation into justification; Melanchthon pushed back on the mechanism.
Gerhard: wider Latin sense of the term is not itself the Pontifical error—Protestants spare Brentius.
